one_month_reasoning: Two events fall in the window. The first is the FY27 Q1 report. Microsoft has not posted the date, but its pattern (Wed Oct 29 2025, Wed Oct 30 2024) points to Oct 28 or 29 after the close, before the Oct 30 scoring close. The Sep 2 8-K guide is revenue of $89.85-90.95B, Azure +44-45% cc on the new definition and capex over $50B. The second is the Oct 27-28 FOMC. After the soft Sep 30 PCE print, swaps price about a 36% chance of a hike, down from roughly even, and the Sep 30 close already reflects that. Copilot seat momentum (30M+, net adds more than doubling quarter on quarter) and the week's run-up leave the earnings reaction two-sided. The market will focus on capex, which will grow in FY27, and on the RPO mix, since OpenAI is about 40% of RPO. I keep a near-neutral lognormal: median about $520, one-month sigma about 9.5% (32%/3.5 plus a little for earnings). The update from round 1 is negligible.

fair_value.method: Blended $563: P/E 50% ($570 = NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of $23.75 x 24x), SOTP 35% ($570 = core $546 at 23x NTM EPS, plus a 25% OpenAI stake at about $1.1T less a 25% haircut, $28/share, less $4/share of net debt including finance leases), and a lease-adjusted FCF-yield cross-check 15% ($525).

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus of $23.68 less about 3% for server depreciation (2-6 year lives) from capex that keeps growing in FY27. The building useful-life change gives only a 'minimal' FY27 operating-income benefit. The 2026 layoffs and hiring freeze support management's guide of FY27 margin down less than 1 point, so I do not cut deeper.
FY28 $23.0 grown about 13%, below FY26's 23% non-GAAP growth because depreciation keeps rising.

Today's NTM multiple is about 25x (518 / (0.75 x 19.76 + 0.25 x 23.68) = 25.0x). I assume about 1 turn of compression for capex fatigue and OpenAI concentration (about 40% of RPO; any-cloud rights since Apr 2026).

inputs_detail.derivation: The core trades at about 23.7x NTM today ((518 - 28) / 20.74). I apply the same one-turn-or-less compression as in the P/E leg.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 lease-adjusted FCF about $75B at a 2.0% yield = $3.75T, which is $504/share, plus the $28 stake, less $4 net debt, about $525 after rounding

inputs_detail.input: FY26 operating cash flow / cash capex

inputs_detail.derivation: OCF grows about 18% a year to roughly $255B. Capex including datacenter leases is roughly $180B: FY27 capex grows year on year, and about $15B a year now sits in operating leases, which flatters reported FCF, so I add it back to capex. The $329B of uncommenced leases runs FY27-FY33.
The current FCF yield is under 2% during the build-out. I assume it stays near 2% in a year.

bear.story: Azure slows into the low 30s as capacity catches up, and OpenAI (about 40% of the $678B RPO, now free to use any cloud) moves incremental spend to AWS or Oracle. Depreciation and lease costs from the $329B uncommenced stack squeeze margins, FY28 EPS comes in around $20.5 and the multiple falls to about 19x, a revisit of the April-2026 low.

base.story: Azure grows 38-45%, Copilot paid seats go from 30M toward 55-60M (about 7% of 450M commercial seats today), M365 commercial cloud grows high-teens, FY27 margin is down less than 1 point, NTM EPS is about $23.75 and the multiple is about 24x, plus the stake.

bull.story: Azure stays above 45%, Copilot doubles and lifts M365 ARPU, OpenAI closes at $1.4T or more (the stake is worth about $47/share gross), capex growth flattens in FY28, and the stock rerates to about 28x on $24.5 EPS.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $390 (roughly 17x my FY28 EPS of $23.0 and 20x FY27 consensus, about 25% below today) the stock would be back at the April-2026 capex-scare zone. Holding there would most likely mean something fundamental broke: Azure below about 30%, OpenAI repricing or shifting its RPO commitment under its any-cloud rights, or capex rising while revenue guidance falls. The supervisor uses $400. I keep $390 because the stock already traded near $349-416 in 2026 with earnings intact, so the $390-400 zone can come from multiple compression alone. Judge the break on estimate cuts, not price alone.

key_uncertainties: The true FY27 capex including operating-lease datacenter spend (the ~$175B is calendar 2026, and FY27 grows year on year), and how fast server depreciation eats margin
OpenAI concentration: about 40% of RPO and $24.1B (7.3%) of FY26 revenue, with any-cloud rights since Apr 2026
Whether Copilot seat growth (30M, only about 7% of 450M seats) turns into M365 ARPU, given that consumer Copilot web share is stuck at about 1.6% (Similarweb, Aug 2026)
OpenAI valuation path ($852B closed, $1.4T under discussion) and IPO timing
Rates: October hike odds about 36% after PCE
reasoning: Round 2 applies the supervisor's fact-checks. (1) The stake is about 25% as-converted per the 10-K, not 27%. I now value it off the $852B closed round and the preliminary ~$1.4T talks (about $1.1T midpoint, less 25%, about $28/share) rather than prediction-market IPO odds, which I have dropped. (2) The ~$175B is calendar-2026 capex, and FY27 capex grows year on year, with about $15B moved to operating leases. I therefore added a lease-adjusted FCF-yield cross-check ($525, 15% weight) and cut the whole-company multiple from 25x to 24x. (3) OpenAI is about 40% of RPO, so I widened the bear case to 22% probability at $385. (4) I now subtract net debt including finance leases (about -$4/share). (5) I moved to NTM EPS of $23.75 (FY28 $23.0, a 3% haircut to the confirmed $23.68 consensus), which is slightly above my old $22.9 and partly offsets the rest. I followed up in my lane. The TD Cowen lease-cancellation reports trace to Feb-Mar 2025 (DCD, Investing.com, Data Center Frontier), so they are stale and I no longer use them as a current signal. The $329B uncommenced-lease note is the better read. Similarweb's Aug-2026 tracker puts Copilot at 1.6% of gen-AI web traffic against 2.0% a year earlier, so Microsoft's consumer AI position is weak and the value sits in enterprise seats and Azure. I tie Copilot to a number: 30M paid seats is about a $10B run-rate (about $30/seat/month) and 7% of 450M M365 seats, and doubling seats would add roughly 8-10 points to M365 commercial cloud growth over time, so the ~+17% guide is achievable, not a stretch. 2026 layoffs (about 4,800) and a hiring freeze outside AI back management's guide of FY27 margin down less than 1 point. The blended fair value is $563 (was $570) and the scenario mean is about $562. The ladder is a mixture: 90% lognormal with median $557 and sigma 0.285, plus 10% capex-bust lognormal with median $400. P(>= $518) moves from 0.575 to 0.556. The 1-month ladder is almost unchanged (median about $520, sigma 9.5%). Research was limited to 5 new searches, and X posts were not fetched directly.
